headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and compliance risk when paired with a non-networked but unverified open-source agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and web content, so attacker-controlled text can reach its tool-use path; awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no shared channel, so direct hijack is not shown. The pairwise pathway is inferred from open-webui’s documented surfaces, not from direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to an MCP server or file source containing untrusted content, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF awesome-nlp output is manually copied into open-webui prompts, injected instructions can be reintroduced.
mitigations: Disable MCP and file ingestion for untrusted sources.
Add a strict instruction/content separator in prompts.
Require human review before tool execution.
Use allowlisted connectors only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches files, documents, notes, API keys, and persistent memory, while awesome-nlp is open-source and non-runnable with no egress. The pair can still leak data if shared files or prompts move sensitive content into open-webui’s broader storage and API surfaces; the uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local files or mounted volume, data can flow from awesome-nlp inputs into open-webui storage.
IF open-webui is configured with external APIs, files from the shared workspace may be transmitted off-box.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Remove secrets from shared directories.
Turn off external API connectors.
Restrict open-webui file uploads to approved paths.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the mounted volume.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or runtime surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources; open-webui does have files and persistent sessions, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority in the profiles. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration beyond the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF an operator manually gives awesome-nlp a writable workspace outside the profile, write conflicts could emerge.
IF open-webui is deployed with the same mounted volume as another writer, session or file contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp read-only.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid sharing git or database state.
Lock shared files during edits.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on tool outputs and persistent memory, so if it treats awesome-nlp-derived text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. awesome-nlp itself is only a repository/listing and does not verify or correct those outputs, so the pair lacks a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp content is pasted into open-webui as facts or citations, open-webui may render or act on them without verification.
IF open-webui tools are enabled, downstream actions can be triggered from unverified text.
mitigations: Require source links for all claims.
Add a verification step before tool calls.
Disable action-taking tools for untrusted inputs.
Mark imported text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: implement citation validation against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, persistent memory, and analytics, while awesome-nlp is an open-source repo with no stated compliance controls. The pair creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated data is routed into open-webui’s broader storage or third-party APIs; the evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are entered into open-webui, retention and third-party processing obligations apply.
IF open-webui is deployed outside the required residency or DPA boundary, compliance breach risk increases.
mitigations: Block regulated data in open-webui.
Review retention settings.
Disable analytics for sensitive deployments.
Confirm DPA and residency settings.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification enforcement.
